results.summary: Let $p\ne q$ be odd primes. Then \mu_p=[p\equiv3,5\pmod8],$$ and $[ab/p]=[a/p]+[b/p]$ for integers $a,b$ prime to $p$ (so the bit of a finite product of integers prime to $p$ is the sum of their bits). For $a$ prime to $p$, $[a/p]=0$ if and only if $(a/p)=1$; more generally, for $b\in\mathbb F_2$, $[a/p]=b$ if and only if $(a/p)=(-1)^b$. A prime $q\ne p$ is prime to $p$.

results.title: The configuration of an odd number and Selmer certificates
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $(f_k)_{k\in K}$ be a finite family of distinct odd primes. Its *configuration* has the symbols $K$, the classes $c_k=f_k\bmod 8$ and the bits $[f_a/f_b]$ (the residue bit of $f_a$ modulo $f_b$); reciprocity is quadratic reciprocity in residue bits. For an odd positive integer $d$, the configuration $\mathcal C_d$ of $d$ is that of the primes dividing $d$.

results.summary: A rational $B$ is *admissible* if its reduced denominator is a square, $0<B<1/2$, and $v_p(B)\ge4$ for every $p\in S_0=\{2,3,5,7,13\}$. These are the hypotheses of pole completeness, which therefore says that every admissible $B$ satisfies $\Phi(B)$.

results.title: The multiplier lemma
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: Let $B$ be a nonzero rational. Then there is a positive divisor $m$ of $2730$ such that $\beta=\mathrm{sqf}(mB)$ is odd and $|\beta|\equiv7\pmod8$. In particular every admissible $B$ has a signed divisor $m$ of $2730$ with $\beta$ odd and $|\beta|\equiv7\pmod8$.

results.title: The slot lemma
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: Let $S$ be a finite set of odd primes with signs $\varepsilon_p\in\{\pm1\}$ ($p\in S$), let $a$ be an odd integer and $A$ a finite set of natural numbers. Then there is a prime $q\notin A$ with $q\equiv a\pmod8$ and $(q/p)=\varepsilon_p$ for every $p\in S$.

results.title: Pole completeness from the certified rank hypothesis
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Assume the certified rank hypothesis CR₃. Then pole completeness holds: every admissible $B$ satisfies $\Phi(B)$, for the pole polynomial with the congruent number curves $y^2=x(x-\ell)(x+\ell)$.
